name: neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
def: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis is a disorder of the eccrine sweat glands that usually develops 7-14 days after initiating chemotherapy. It is generally regarded as a cytotoxic process directed at the sweat glands, e.g. via a direct toxic effect of chemotherapeutic drugs that are excreted in the sweat.

name: grover's disease
def: Grover's Disease results in small red, bumpy spots (papules) on the central back, mid chest and occasionally elsewhere. The cause is unknown. Sometimes, it follows sweating or some unexpected heat stress, so there has been suspicion that it may relate to the sweat ducts in some way. But it also may arise in quite dry skin. Many affected individuals are sun damaged.

name: generalized hypertrichosis
def: Generalized hypertrichosis is the presence of lanugo hair, excess vellus hair, or terminal hair on much of the cutaneous surface, including an acquired transformation of terminal hair into lanugo hair.

name: congenital hypertrichosis lanuginosa
def: This is a rare autosomal dominant disease in which lanugo hair is not replaced by normal vellus hair. The fine, silvery-gray to blond hair continues to grow, reaching lengths of up to 10 cm and covering the entire body surface except for the palms, soles, dorsal surface of the distal phalanges, and prepuce. The hair growth is said to lead to a dog or monkey face. Associated dental abnormalities, malformations of the ear, glaucoma, pyloric stenosis, photophobia, and, rarely, physical and mental retardation have been reported.

name: pressure ulcer stage 1
def: Non-blanchable erythema of intact skin which heralds skin ulceration. For darker-skinned individuals, warmth, edema, discoloration of the skin and induration may serve as indicators of impending ulceration.

name: pressure ulcer stage 2
def: Partial-thickness skin loss involving the epidermis, dermis or both. This superficial lesion presents as an erosion, blister or shallow ulcer.

name: pressure ulcer stage 3
def: Full-thickness skin loss with damage to the subcutaneous tissue, extending down to (but not including) the underlying fascia. This deep lesion presents as a crater-like ulcer and sometimes involves adjacent tissue.

name: pressure ulcer stage 4
def: Full-thickness skin loss and extensive tissue necrosis with destruction extending to muscle, bone, or supporting structures such as tendons or joint capsules. Undermining or sinus tracts can be present.

The etiology of this entity is not known, but a viral etiology has been proposed due to the detection of intranuclear viral particles by electron microscopy.

def: An acneiform eruption that occurs in newborns or infants, and is often seen on the nose and adjacent portions of the cheek.

name: closed comedone acne
def: A type of acne lesion, which develops when plugs of skin cells and oil become trapped within the hair follicle and the pore opening is obstructed.

name: open comedone acne
def: Acne with dome-shaped papules showing a conspicuous dilated follicular opening that is filled with an inspissated core of shed keratin.

name: acneiform eruption
def: Visible efflorescent lesions of the skin caused by acne or resembling acne.

name: cystic acne
def: Form of acne where cysts are deeper and filled with a combination of pus and serosanguineous fluid. In patients with severe nodulocystic acne, these lesions frequently coalesce to form large, complex inflamed plaques that can include sinus tracts.

name: post-adolescent acne
def: Inflammatory acne persisting beyond 25 years of age which typically features tender, deep-seated papulonodules on the lower third of the face, jawline and neck.

name: acne fulminans
def: Severe scarring acne associated with fever, polyarthralgia, crusted ulcerative lesions, weight loss, and anemia.

name: acne conglobata
def: Very severe and chronic form of acne vulgaris in which inflammatory lesions predominate and run together and often forming exudates or bleeding.

name: follicular occlusion tetrad
def: The combination of major acne, pilonidal sinus, chronic scalp folliculitis, and hidradenitis suppurativa.
synonyms: dissecting cellulitis of the scalp, hidradenitis suppurativa and pilonidal cysts, and acne conglobata

def: A complication of acne vulgaris  with distortion of the midline face and cheeks due to soft tissue swelling.

name: rosacea
def: Rosacea is a chronic red rash involving the central face.

name: erythematotelangiectatic rosacea
def: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea is a term that covers individuals who have a tendency for flushing, combined with a background of persistent facial erythema and sometimes telangiectasias.

name: papulopustular rosacea
def: Papulopustular rosacea is characterized by a centrofacial eruption of multiple, small (<3 mm), dome-shaped, erythematous papules, some of which are surmounted by a seropustule.

name: phymatous rosacea
def: Rosacea involving hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands of the affected region.

name: ocular rosacea
def: Ocular rosacea may of may not be accompanied by cutaneous signs. Ocular rosacea may be characterized by chronically bloodshot eyes, dry eyes, blepharitis, tiny concretions at the bases of the cilia, or mild scaling of the eyelid margins.

name: rhinophyma
def: Rhinophyma is a hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands in nasal skin.
synonyms: hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands in nasal skin

name: erythematotelangiectatic rosacea stage 1
def: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea is a term that covers individuals who have a tendency for flushing, combined with a background of persistent facial erythema and sometimes telangiectasias. Characterized by occasional mild flushing; faint persistent centrofacial erythema; few telangiectasias.

name: erythematotelangiectatic rosacea stage 2
def: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea is a term that covers individuals who have a tendency for flushing, combined with a background of persistent facial erythema and sometimes telangiectasias. Characterized by frequent troublesome flushing; moderate persistent centrofacial erythema; several distinct telangiectasias.

name: erythematotelangiectatic rosacea stage 3
def: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea is a term that covers individuals who have a tendency for flushing, combined with a background of persistent facial erythema and sometimes telangiectasias. Characterized by frequent severe flushing; pronounced persistent centrofacial erythema; many prominent telangiectasias; possible edema.

name: ocular rosacea stage 1
def: Ocular rosacea may of may not be accompanied by cutaneous signs. Ocular rosacea may be characterized by chronically bloodshot eyes, dry eyes, blepharitis, tiny concretions at the bases of the cilia, or mild scaling of the eyelid margins. Defined by mild itch, dryness or grittiness; fine scaling of eyelid margins; telangiectasia of eyelid margins; mild conjunctival injection.

name: ocular rosacea stage 2
def: Ocular rosacea may of may not be accompanied by cutaneous signs. Ocular rosacea may be characterized by chronically bloodshot eyes, dry eyes, blepharitis, tiny concretions at the bases of the cilia, or mild scaling of the eyelid margins. Defined by burning or stinging; crusting, irregularity, erythema and/or edema of eyelid margins; definite conjunctival injection; chalazion or hordeolum.

name: ocular rosacea stage 3
def: Ocular rosacea may of may not be accompanied by cutaneous signs. Ocular rosacea may be characterized by chronically bloodshot eyes, dry eyes, blepharitis, tiny concretions at the bases of the cilia, or mild scaling of the eyelid margins. Defined by pain, photosensitivity, blurred vision; severe eyelid changes with loss of lashes, severe conjunctival inflammation; corneal changes, with potential loss of vision; episcleritis, scleritis; iritis.

name: papulopustular rosacea stage 1
def: Papulopustular rosacea is characterized by a centrofacial eruption of multiple, small (<3 mm), dome-shaped, erythematous papules, some of which are surmounted by a seropustule. Stage 1 defined by few papules and/or papulopustules; mild persistent centrofacial erythema.

name: papulopustular rosacea stage 2
def: Papulopustular rosacea is characterized by a centrofacial eruption of multiple, small (<3 mm), dome-shaped, erythematous papules, some of which are surmounted by a seropustule. Stage 2 defined by sseveral papules and/or papulopustules; moderate persistent centrofacial erythema.

name: papulopustular rosacea stage 3
def: Papulopustular rosacea is characterized by a centrofacial eruption of multiple, small (<3 mm), dome-shaped, erythematous papules, some of which are surmounted by a seropustule. Stage 3 defined by extensive papules and/or papulopustules; pronounced persistent centrofacial erythema; inflammatory plaques or edema may be present.

name: phymatous rosacea stage 1
def: Rosacea involving hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands of the affected region. Stage1  characterized by puffiness; mildly patulous follicles; no clinically apparent hypertrophy of connective tissue or sebaceous glands; no change in contour.

name: phymatous rosacea stage 2
def: Rosacea involving hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands of the affected region. Stage 2 characterized by moderate swelling; moderately dilated patulous follicles; clinically, mild hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands or connective tissue; change in nasal contour without nodular component.

name: phymatous rosacea stage 3
def: Rosacea involving hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands of the affected region. Stage 3 characterized by marked swelling; large dilated follicles; distortion of contour due to hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands and/or connective tissue, with a nodular component.

name: gnathophyma
def: hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands of the central chin.

name: otophyma
def: Hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands, causing swelling of the ears, primarily affecting the lower half of the helices and the lobes of the ears.

name: mentophyma
def: Cushion-like, firm swelling of central forehead, caused by hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands.

name: blepharophyma
def: Hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands of the eyelids, leading to swelling of the eyelids.

name: rosacea fulminans
def: Rosacea fulminans is characterized by the explosive onset of inflammatory papules and pustules superimposed on a background of facial erythema and sometimes even accompanied by fever.

name: granulomatous rosacea
def: Persistent red-brown to skin-colored facial papules with a characteristic non-caseating granulomatous histology is referred to as granulomatous rosacea.

name: rosacea-like disorder
def: Disorder presenting like rosacea.

name: periorificial dermatitis
def: Periorificial dermatitis, has a superficial resemblance to rosacea but the morphology of the lesions - grouped tiny superficial papulovesicles or papulopustules in the same stage of development rather than larger crops of papules and pustules in varying stages of development - and the distribution of the lesions usually indicate the correct diagnosis.

name: rosaceiform dermatitis
def: Rosaceiform dermatitis refers to a drug eruption caused by the application of topical calcineurin inhibitors to the face. It is characterized by facial erythema, small papules and numerous pustules.

name: steroid-induced rosacea
def: Steroid-induced rosacea presents with erythema, papules, pustules and sometimes telangiectasias and atrophy due to repeated applications of potent topical corticosteroid preparations to the face.

name: pityriasis folliculorum
def: Pityriasus fulliculorum is characerized by a roughened, whitish, scaling skin surface  superimposed on a background of faint erythema plus scattered fine papules and pustules. It is thought to be caused in young to middle-aged women by the patients rarely allowing water to contact the skin of their face and continually apply moisturizing creams and cosmetic preparations.

name: haber's syndrome
def: Haber's syndrome is a rare familial genodermatosis characterized by early-onset facial erythema, verrucous papules, truncal keratotic lesions and pitted atrophic scars.

name: follicular disorder
def: Disorder of the hair follicles.

name: folliculitis
def: Infection of the hair follicles.

name: superficial folliculitis
def: Infection of the hair follicles, limited to only the superficial follicles.

name: sycosis lupoid
def: Scarring form of deep folliculitis, typically affecting the beard area; may be caused by S. aureus, chronic course, refractory to treatment.

name: irritant folliculitis
def: Follicular pustules in the sites of application or exposure to irritant, often after application of topical medications.

name: dermatophyte folliculitis
def: Folliculitis caused by infection of a dermatophyte fungus.

name: majocchi's granuloma
def: Majocchi granuloma is a deep and persistent suppurative folliculitis caused by dermatophyte fungi.

name: candida folliculitis
def: Pruritic satellite pustules surrounding areas of intertriginous candidiasis.

name: demodex folliculitis
def: Erythematous follicular papules and pustules on the face, often with a background of diffuse erythema. Skin scrapings reveal numerous Demodex mites.

name: drug-induced folliculitis
def: Acute eruption of monomorphic erythematous follicular papules and pustules on the trunk, shoulders and upper arms after exposure to a therapeutic agent.

name: actinic folliculitits
def: Development of follicular pustules on the upper trunk and arms 24-30 hours after first sun exposure of the summer.

name: eosinophilic folliculitis
def: Eosinophilic folliculitis is a recurrent skin disorder of unknown cause. Histological specimens find eosinophils around hair follicle.

name: eosiniphilic pustular folliculitis
def: Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis is characterized by recurrent episodes of eruptive, intensely pruritic, follicular papulopustules.

name: AIDS-associated eosinophilic folliculitis
def: A pruritic papular eruption with histologic features that are similar to eosinophilic pustular folliculitis can develop in HIV-infected patients, many of whom fulfill the criteria for AIDS.

name: disseminate and recurrent infundibulofolliculitis
def: Hundreds of uniform, skin-colored papules that have been likened to goose bumps. Histologically, there is mild inflammation of the follicular infundibulum.
synonyms: hitch and lund disease|recurrent disseminated infundibulofolliculitits

name: erythromelanosis follicularis faciei
def: A follicular disorder that involves the lateral cheeks and sometimes the lateral aspects of the neck. Multiple pinpoint follicular papules are superimposed on a red-brown patch; the papules appear relatively hypopigmented.

name: keratosis pilaris atrophicans
def: Keratosis pilaris atrophicans encompasses a group of disorders in which the abnormality in follicular keratinization is accompanied by atrophy and scarring alopecia.

name: keratosis pilaris atrophicans faciei
def: Facial follicular atrophy.
xrefs: SNOMEDCT_US_2015_03_01:7719008 "keratosis pilaris atrophicans faciei"|DERMLEX:2329 "keratosis pilaris atrophicans faciei"

name: atrophoderma vermiculatum
def: Facial follicular atrophy, resulting in severe worm-eaten appearance of the cheeks.
synonyms: acne vermoulante|atrophoderma reticulata symmertica faciei|folliculitis ulerythema reticulata|folliculitis ulerythemosa|honeycomb atrophy|ulerythema acneiforme

name: folliculitits spinulosa decalvans
def: Facial follicular atrophy which results in bald areas on the scalp due to follicular pustules.

name: phrynoderma
def: Follicular papules of various sizes with conical keratotic plugs favor the extensor surfaces of the extremities, but may then spread to involve other locations. The face is the last site to become involved, and the hands and feet are spared.

name: deep folliculitis
def: Infection of the hair follicles, also affecting the deeper structures of the skin.

name: sycosis
def: Infection of the bearded part of a man's face, caused by a bacterial infection.

name: mycotic sycosis
def: Dermatophyte folliculitis of the beard area (most often the chin), usually caused by zoophilic organisms.

name: herpetic sycosis
def: Rapid development of individual and grouped follicular pustules and vesicles on an erythematous base in the beard area, due to spread of herpes simplex virus spread to the area.

name: pseudofolliculitits barbae
def: Pseudofolliculitis barbae is a common chronic inflammatory disorder occurring most often in the beard area of men who shave.
synonyms: barber's itch|chronic sycosis barbae|follulitis barbae traumatica|ingrown hairs|razor bumps|scarring pseudofolliculitits of the beard|shave bumps

name: hidradenitis suppurativa
def: Hidradenitis suppurativa targets apocrine gland-bearing skin sites, in particular the axillae and anogenital region. It is a chronic condition characterized by recurrent furuncles and draining sinus tracts with subsequent scarring.

name: hidradenitis suppurativa stage 1
def: Hidradenitis suppurativa with one or more abscesses with no sinus tract or scar formation.

name: hidradenitis suppurativa stage 2
def: Hidradenitis suppurativa with one or more widely separated recurrent abscesses, with sinus tract and scar formation.

name: hidradenitis suppurativa stage 3
def: Hidradenitis suppurativa with multiple interconnected tracts and abscesses throughout an affected region.

name: trichostasis spinulosa
def: Trichostasis spinulosa is a common but often underdiagnosed follicular disorder of unknown etiology. Asymptomatic comedo-like lesions that contain keratin and multiple vellus hairs are seen.

name: disorder of the eccrine or apocrine sweat gland
hyperhidrosis
def: Hyperhidrosis is the name given to excessive and uncontrollable sweating.

name: primary hyperhidrosis
def: Primary hyperhidrosis is defined as excessive sweating in localized areas that is not associated with a systemic disorder.

name: volar hyperhidrosis
def: Primary hyperhidrosis localized to the palms of the hands and soles of the feet.

name: axillary hyperhidrosis
def: Primary hyperhidrosis localized to the axillae.

name: secondary hyperhidrosis
def: Secondary hyperhidrosis is caused by or associated with another systemic disorder.

name: hypothalamic hyperhidrosis
def: Hyperhidrosis due to elevated body temperature or direct hypothalamic stimulation. May be nocturnal or diurnal.

name: drug-induced hyperhidrosis
def: Increased sweating due to the pharmacological effects of certain drugs after administration.

name: physiological medullary hyperhidrosis
def: Physiologic medullary hyperhidrosis is most commonly triggered by spicy foods, alcohol and citrus fruits.

name: pathological medullary hyperhidrosis
def: This disorder arises after disruption of nerves. During healing, nerve fibers mediating sweating aberrantly connect to nerves that mediate salivation. Impulses in parasympathetic fibers normally supplying the salivary glands are now misdirected to the sweat glands. As a result, salivary stimulation elicits sweating.

name: auriculotemporal syndrome
def: Auriculotemporal syndrome is common after parotid surgery, presenting with gustatory flushing, but usually no obvious sweating.

name: chorda tympani syndrome
def: This disorder results from transposition of sympathetic sudomotor and parasympathetic secretomotor fibers to the submandibular gland that are carried in the chorda tympani nerve. In this syndrome, salivary stimuli induce sweating on the chin and lower jaw line.

name: spinal sweating
def: Any injury or disease process that severs or interferes with the reticulospinal tracts of the cord can disrupt the sweating reflex. A lack of sweating in response to thermal stimulation usually occurs below the level of the injury.

name: autonomic dysreflexia
def: Autonomic dysreflexia is a syndrome that may occur with spinal injury at or above T6. Massive episodic sympathetic discharge results in sweating above the level of the transection accompanied by headache, hypertension, facial flushing, bradycardia or tachycardia, piloerection and paresthesias.

name: compensatory hyperhidrosis
def: The sweat glands of one area become hyperactive in an effort to compensate for hypo- or anhidrosis, caused by denervation or disease, in another.

name: non-neural hyperhidrosis
def: Direct stimulation of eccrine sweat glands by heat or sudomimetic drugs can lead to localized sweating.

name: hypohidrosis
def: Reduced sweating.

name: central hypohidrosis
def: Disruption of the central sweating centres of the brain resulting in decreased or absent sweating.

name: neuropathic hypohidrosis
def: Disruption of the innervation of the sweat glands at any level below the central nervous system leading to reduced or absent sweating.

name: anhidrosis
def: Inability to produce sweat

name: drug-induced anhidrosis
def: Anhidrosis induced by drug administration, often with anticholinergic effects.

name: drug-induced hypohidrosis
def: Reduced sweating due to the pharmacological effects of certain drugs after administration.

name: miliaria
def: Disorder due to obstruction of the eccrine sweat gland.

name: miliaria crystallina
def: Disorder due to obstruction of the eccrine sweat gland at the level of the stratum corneum.

name: miliaria rubra
def: Disorder due to obstruction of the eccrine sweat gland at the level of the mid-epidermis.

name: miliaria profunda
def: Disorder due to obstruction of the eccrine sweat gland at the level of the dermal-epidermal junction.

name: congenital miliaria crystallina
def: Disorder due to obstruction of the eccrine sweat gland at the level of the stratum corneum. Pre-natal aetiology.

name: miliaria pustulosa
def: Disorder due to obstruction of the eccrine sweat gland leading to inflammation and bacterial infection.

name: eccrine bromhidrosis
def: Bromhidrosis is a condition of abnormal or offensive body odour, originating from the eccrine sweat glands.

name: eccrine chromhidrosis
def: Eccrine chromhidrosis refers to the secretion of pigmented/coloured sweat.

name: apocrine chromhidrosis
def: Apocrine chromhidrosis refers to the secretion of pigmented (yellow, green or black) sweat. It is a reflection of the rich lipofuscin content of apocrine sweat.

name: skin disease with sweat as a predisposing influence
granulosis rubra nasi
def: Rare inherited condition where hyperhidrosis of the nose is followed by macular erythema; papules and vesicles can also develop. The process may extend to the cheeks, lips and upper chin.

name: keratolysis exfoliativa
def: Keratolysis exfoliativa is a common, asymptomatic, superficial desquamative process of palmar and (less often) plantar skin; it usually worsens in warm weather and is occasionally associated with hyperhidrosis. Keratolysis exfoliativa is seen in healthy adults and probably reflects low-grade physical or chemical damage to the thick stratum corneum of volar skin.
synonyms: dyshidrosis lamellosa sicca|lamellar dyshidrosis|recurrent focal palmar peeling

name: multiple sweat gland abcesses
def: Multiple sweat gland abscesses represent a rare disorder of newborn infants that is likely due to a secondary staphylococcal infection of miliaria lesions.

name: apocrine sweat gland disorder
def: Disorder of the appocrine sweat gland.

name: fox-fordyce disease
def: Fox-Fordyce disease is characterised by the development of itchy bumps around the hair follicles of the underarm area, pubic region, and/or around the nipples. It results from inflammation of the aprocrine sweat glands, which are found only in these areas.
